annotations.description: Check the app behind the router first: a 502 or 504 here is Traefik answering for a backend that is down or refusing the port. A 500 that is steady across several routers means the router itself is broken. The dashboard panel '5xx share by router' carries the same numbers. The router label is namespace/template-hash, so the name is the route's IngressRoute, not the hostname: get it with kubectl get ingressroute -A | grep <name>.
annotations.summary: Traefik router {{ $labels.router }} is failing more than 10 % of its requests

model.expr: (sum by (router) (rate(traefik_router_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) / clamp_min(sum by (router) (rate(traefik_router_requests_total[5m])), 0.001) > 0.10) and on(router) (sum by (router) (rate(traefik_router_requests_total[5m])) > 0.01)

annotations.description: The router itself adds microseconds; a p95 this high means the backend is slow or queueing. Compare with the app's own request duration before touching Traefik. Threshold is provisional: the busiest router averaged 76 ms on 2026-11-21, and the buckets were only widened that day, so re-tune after a week of real p95. Panel 'p95 and p99 latency by router' has the shape, and the 99th percentile separates 'one slow endpoint' from 'everything is slow'.
annotations.summary: Traefik router {{ $labels.router }} has a p95 above 1 s

model.expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, router) (rate(traefik_router_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) > 1) and on(router) (sum by (router) (rate(traefik_router_requests_total[5m])) > 0.01)
sum(count_over_time({job="fluent-bit", container="traefik"} |~ "does not exist|nonexistent certificate resolver|invalid rule|error while building|failed to load" [15m]))

annotations.description: Traefik logged a dynamic-configuration error — a Middleware, IngressRoute or certificate resolver it could not resolve. The router keeps serving the last good configuration, so the routes may still answer while the object you just applied is not in effect; the log line is the evidence. Read it with `kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/traefik --tail=100`. This rule counts the router's own configuration-error lines in Loki over 15 minutes, because Traefik v3 exposes no reload-failure counter and advances `traefik_config_last_reload_success` even when part of the configuration fails to build. The old no-successful-reload-in-24-h branch was removed on 2026-11-28: it fired after 29 quiet hours on a healthy router, because a cluster with no route changes legitimately reloads nothing. It does not cover a Helm values file that fails to render, which never reaches Traefik, or an unreachable /metrics endpoint, which ScrapeTargetDown owns.
